Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure requires only **one** A1c in the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

For **MY2026**, the eGFR value set is modernized to the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 estimating equation and
**drops the legacy race-based (MDRD) eGFR code** that older lab feeds still emit. Health systems whose result
feed still carries the legacy code will see eGFR coverage — and therefore KED compliance — fall on otherwise
unchanged data until mapping is updated. This is the second controlled drift scenario in the demo.

Genie Ontology Page — Care Gap (Numerator, Denominator, MET / NOT_MET)
HEDIS measures are expressed as a **denominator** and a **numerator**, and compliance is the ratio.

- **Denominator (eligible):** the patients a measure applies to (e.g. the diabetes cohort in an age band).
- **Numerator (compliant):** the eligible patients who received the required care (e.g. an A1c test for GSD;
  both eGFR and uACR for KED).
- **Status:** a patient is **MET** when in the numerator, otherwise **NOT_MET** — a **care gap** (eligible but
  missing the required care). Closing care gaps raises the measure's compliance rate.
- **Compliance rate** = compliant ÷ eligible, exposed as a governed measure in the metric views
  (`GSD Compliance Rate`, `KED Compliance Rate`). Each gold row keeps **record-level evidence** (the test
  date/code/value) so a gap, or a met status, is fully traceable.

> HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

whether patients with diabetes had their glycemic status evaluated during the measurement year.

**GSD Compliance Rate** in `gsd_compliance_metrics` (compliant ÷ eligible).

Genie Ontology Page — KED — Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes
**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure for assessing kidney
health in diabetic patients. Its numerator is **compound** — it requires two different tests in the same year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–85** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** **both** of the following in the measurement year:
  1. an **eGFR** (estimated glomerular filtration rate) test — value set `KED_EGFR`, and
  2. a **uACR** (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) test — value set `KED_UACR`.

A patient is **MET** only when **both** components are present; missing either is a care gap. Because the two
components are tracked separately, the **eGFR Test Rate** and **uACR Test Rate** are each exposed in
`ked_compliance_metrics` alongside the combined **KED Compliance Rate**. In this demo uACR is the limiting
component (eGFR ~92%, uACR ~51%, combined ~51%).

> The eGFR value set spans LOINC vintages (e.g. `33914-3` MDRD and `98979-8`) — a reminder that value sets
> evolve and a measure must accept all valid codes for the concept. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

Genie Ontology Page — Diabetes Cohort
The **diabetes cohort** is the set of patients with a diabetes diagnosis, used as the basis for the diabetes
quality measures (GSD, KED, etc.). It is resolved **semantically**, not by a hand-maintained code list.

- A patient is in the cohort if they have any ICD-10-CM diagnosis that is a **descendant of E10, E11, or
  E13** (type 1, type 2, and other/specified diabetes) in the ICD-10 hierarchy.
- This is computed by joining `silver_condition` to the **`icd10_closure`** table on `descendant_code` where
  `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')` — a **single equality join** that captures the entire subtree
  (e.g. `E11.21`, `E11.319`) via **subsumption**.
- Result: `silver_diabetes_cohort` (distinct `patient_id`). A flat code list would miss specific children and
  undercount; the hierarchy closure catches them all.

> See also **ICD-10 Subsumption**. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

Genie Ontology Page — SPD — Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes
**SPD (Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS measure for statin use in diabetic patients.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **40–75** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** dispensed **at least one statin** during the measurement year.

**Why this exercises the ontology:** the `SPD_STATIN` value set lists RxNorm **ingredients** (e.g. `36567`
simvastatin, `83367` atorvastatin), but prescriptions carry RxNorm **clinical-drug** codes (e.g. `312961`
*Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet*). A flat match of ingredients against prescriptions finds **zero** statins.
SPD instead resolves statins by **subsumption over `rxnorm_closure`** (ingredient → its clinical drugs) — the
same closure-join pattern used for the diabetes cohort over ICD-10. This is the medication-side companion to
ICD-10 subsumption: meaning comes from the hierarchy, not a flat code list.

Genie Ontology Page — KED — Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes
**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure for assessing kidney
health in diabetic patients. Its numerator is **compound** — it requires two different tests in the same year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–85** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** **both** of the following in the measurement year:

components are tracked separately, the **eGFR Test Rate** and **uACR Test Rate** are each exposed in

component (eGFR ~92%, uACR ~51%, combined ~51%).

Genie Ontology Page — SPD — Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes
**SPD (Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS measure for statin use in diabetic patients.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **40–75** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** dispensed **at least one statin** during the measurement year.

**Why this exercises the ontology:** the `SPD_STATIN` value set lists RxNorm **ingredients** (e.g. `36567`
simvastatin, `83367` atorvastatin), but prescriptions carry RxNorm **clinical-drug** codes (e.g. `312961`
*Simvastatin 20 MG Oral Tablet*). A flat match of ingredients against prescriptions finds **zero** statins.
SPD instead resolves statins by **subsumption over `rxnorm_closure`** (ingredient → its clinical drugs) — the
same closure-join pattern used for the diabetes cohort over ICD-10. This is the medication-side companion to
ICD-10 subsumption: meaning comes from the hierarchy, not a flat code list.

> HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.
